chapter_summary: Proverbs 21 is a gallery of contrasts between the way of wisdom and the way of folly. It opens with a stunning declaration: God holds the hearts of kings in His hand. It teaches that God sees through self-justification, that justice matters more than empty ritual, and that pride is sin. Hard work, honesty, and generosity are shown to lead to life; laziness, lies, pride, and wickedness lead to ruin. The chapter closes with one of the Bible's most memorable lines: victory does not belong to horses or armies — safety belongs to God alone.
main_lesson: God is in charge of everything — even the hearts of kings. Choosing to do right, be honest, and trust God leads to real life.

memory_verse.kjv: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD.
memory_verse.little_bible: You can get ready. You can prepare everything. But only God can keep you truly safe.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 21 returns to the classic two-path structure of the book: the way of righteousness leads to life; the way of wickedness leads to ruin. But this chapter has a distinctive opening — God directs the king's heart like a river channel. This is a profound truth for children and parents alike: no human authority is outside God's governance. Help your child understand that respecting authority (parents, teachers, leaders) does not mean those authorities are ultimate — God is.

The chapter also has a striking thread about the home: verses 9 and 19 note that a quarrelsome, contentious household is unbearable. This is not a word against women — it is a word about the atmosphere of the home. Peace at home is a treasure. Teach your children that how we speak and act in our home matters enormously.

Verses 25-26 contrast the lazy person (whose hands refuse to work and whose desires kill him) with the righteous person who gives generously. This is a direct application for children — laziness is not just unhelpful, it is destructive. But generosity is the opposite of that death-spiral. Encourage your children to be both diligent and generous.

The final verse is a parenting gift: when your child faces something scary — a test, a performance, a hard situation — remind them that the horse is prepared but safety is of the Lord. We do our best preparation, and we trust God for the outcome.
application_for_children: This week, before something hard or scary, say: 'I will prepare and do my best. But God is the one who keeps me safe.' Then trust Him and do your best.

verses.kjv: The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
verses.little_bible: God holds the king's heart in His hand. He turns it wherever He wants. God is in charge of all rulers.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God guides every king's heart.
verses.meaning: No human authority — not even a king — is outside God's sovereign direction. God governs the hearts of rulers as easily as a farmer channels water in an irrigation ditch. This should produce both humility in rulers and confidence in those they govern: ultimate authority rests with God alone.
verses.prayer: God, You are above every king and ruler.
verses.discussion_question: Who is in charge of the most powerful rulers?
verses.family_discussion: How does knowing that God governs the hearts of leaders help us trust Him even when we are uncertain about those in authority over us?
verses.do_it_today: When you hear about a leader or a rule today, say to yourself: 'God is above them all.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A king on a throne, a vast gentle river flowing beside him, God's hand guiding the water's direction, warm golden watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.
verses.little_bible: Everyone thinks their own choices are right. But God looks deep into every heart. He sees the truth.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: We think we're right. God sees our hearts.
verses.meaning: Self-justification is the natural human default — we evaluate ourselves with a bias toward approval. But God's assessment is not self-reported; He weighs the heart directly. This is both a warning against moral self-deception and a reminder that we need God's perspective, not just our own.
verses.prayer: God, show me where I am wrong.
verses.discussion_question: Can we always trust ourselves to know if we are right?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children move from self-justification to genuine self-examination — inviting God and trusted others to speak truth about their hearts?
verses.do_it_today: Ask someone you trust: 'Is there anything wrong that I cannot see in myself?' Listen without defending.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child looking in a mirror seeing themselves as good, but a gentle divine light looking deeper into their heart with truth, soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
verses.little_bible: Doing what is right and fair is more important to God than offerings. Living rightly matters more than rituals.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Doing right matters more than offerings.
verses.meaning: This verse echoes the prophetic tradition (Micah 6:8; Amos 5:21-24): God desires justice and righteous living over religious performance. Sacrifice without righteous living is unacceptable. This does not abolish worship but insists that worship flows from a life of justice.
verses.prayer: God, help me live rightly, not just look good.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God care about how we treat people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that their everyday choices and treatment of others are a form of worship — not separate from it?
verses.do_it_today: Do one genuinely fair thing today for someone — even if it costs you something.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two scales: one holding an offering, one holding acts of justice and kindness — the justice side glowing with God's pleasure, warm watercolour

verses.kjv: An high look, and a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked, is sin.
verses.little_bible: A proud look and a proud heart are sin. Even the daily work of the wicked is sin. Pride goes all the way through.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pride in the heart is sin.
verses.meaning: Pride contaminates everything — not just proud attitudes but even the ordinary actions ('the plowing') of a proud, wicked person. Sin is not merely what we do in dramatic moments; it colours the whole of a proud person's life. This is a sobering statement about the totality of sin.
verses.prayer: God, take all pride out of my heart.
verses.discussion_question: What does a proud look on a face tell you about that person's heart?
verses.family_discussion: How do we distinguish healthy confidence and God-given dignity from pride that God opposes? How do we cultivate the former and root out the latter in our children?
verses.do_it_today: Watch your face and heart today. If you feel yourself looking down on anyone, stop and pray.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a chin raised proudly, a shadow of sin behind the proud expression, contrasted with a humble child whose face is gentle, soft watercolour

verses.kjv: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
verses.little_bible: Hard work and careful thinking lead to having enough. But rushing and being hasty leads to not having enough.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Diligent thinking leads to plenty.
verses.meaning: Diligence involves not just effort but thoughtful planning — the mind engaged as well as the hands. Haste, by contrast, skips the thinking and rushes into action, producing scarcity. The contrast is between patient, thoughtful industry and reckless rushing.
verses.prayer: God, help me think before I rush.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you rush and do not think things through?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate the combination of thoughtful planning and diligent action in our children — not laziness, but not careless rushing either?
verses.do_it_today: Before starting one task today, spend two minutes planning it. Then work steadily. See the difference.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child planning carefully at a desk with warm light, a full harvest growing beside them; another child rushing and running with empty hands, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.
verses.little_bible: Getting riches by lying is empty and worthless. It leads nowhere good. It is the path of those heading toward destruction.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Riches from lying lead to ruin.
verses.meaning: Wealth gained through deception is characterised as 'vanity' — emptiness, like a vapor — tossed around by those who are actually pursuing death. The lying person thinks they are gaining something; they are actually gaining nothing of value and moving toward their own destruction.
verses.prayer: God, help me never gain anything by lying.
verses.discussion_question: Why is something gained by lying not really worth having?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that the means matter as much as the ends — that how you get something shapes what it actually is?
verses.do_it_today: If you have gained anything today by being less than honest, give it back or make it right.
verses.illustration_prompt: Coins gathered by a lying tongue crumbling into dust and mist, the figure holding them looking shocked, dark contrast watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment.
verses.little_bible: The wicked person takes what is not theirs. That very wrongdoing will destroy them. They refused to do what is right.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wicked choices bring destruction.
verses.meaning: There is a built-in principle of justice in creation: wickedness carries the seed of its own destruction. The wicked refuse to practise judgment — fair dealing and justice — and so their own wrongdoing becomes their ruin.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from taking what is not mine.
verses.discussion_question: Why does doing wrong things end up hurting the one who does them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that God has built consequences into the moral fabric of the world — and that wickedness is ultimately self-defeating?
verses.do_it_today: Is there anything you have that belongs to someone else? Return it today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A hand reaching for something that is not its own, the taking hand caught in a snare that closes around it, solemn watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The way of man is froward and strange: but as for the pure, his work is right.
verses.little_bible: The way of the guilty person is twisted and confusing. But the person who is pure — their work is straight and right.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A pure heart makes work right.
verses.meaning: The contrast is between the twisted, unpredictable path of someone living in guilt or sin and the straight, clear path of someone with a pure heart. Purity of heart produces integrity in action — the inside determines the outside.
verses.prayer: God, make my heart pure and my work right.
verses.discussion_question: How does what is in your heart show up in what you do?
verses.family_discussion: How do we invest in our children's hearts — knowing that heart formation is the root of right behaviour?
verses.do_it_today: Check your heart before you start your main work today. Ask God to make it pure first.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a clear, bright heart doing work that is straight and neat; a shadowed figure whose work is twisted and confused, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
verses.little_bible: It is better to live in a tiny corner of a roof than in a big house full of fighting and quarreling. Peace matters more than space.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Peace at home is better than space.
verses.meaning: This vivid proverb is not a statement against women but against a quarrelsome, contentious spirit in the home. A tiny corner with peace is preferable to a mansion of constant conflict. The lesson is universal: the atmosphere of the home — its emotional and relational climate — matters far more than its size or wealth.
verses.prayer: God, help our home be peaceful.
verses.discussion_question: Why is peace in a home more important than how big the house is?
verses.family_discussion: What is the atmosphere of our home? Are we cultivating peace, or do we allow quarreling to fill the space? What would need to change?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today to bring peace to your home — stop a quarrel, say a kind word, or give a hug.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting peacefully in a tiny corner on a rooftop at sunset, more joyful than someone in a large house where voices are raised in argument, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.
verses.little_bible: The wicked person wants to do evil. They do not care about their neighbour at all. Kindness is not in them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wicked desire evil, not kindness.
verses.meaning: Wickedness is not merely external behaviour — it originates in desire. The wicked person's soul craves evil, and that inward desire shows up in their treatment of neighbours: indifference, hostility, and an absence of kindness. Sin is a heart problem before it is a behaviour problem.
verses.prayer: God, fill my heart with good desires.
verses.discussion_question: How does what we want in our hearts change how we treat people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate righteous desires in our children — not just managing their behaviour but training their hearts to want what is good?
verses.do_it_today: Do one kind thing for a neighbour or friend today — someone you could easily ignore.
verses.illustration_prompt: A dark figure turning away from a neighbour in need, desire for wrong things visible as dark shadows; a bright child turning toward a neighbour with kindness, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
verses.little_bible: When a mocker is punished, even a simple person learns something. And when the wise person is taught, they learn even more.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Punishment teaches the simple. Teaching grows the wise.
verses.meaning: Wisdom can be transmitted in two ways: observation of consequences (seeing a mocker punished makes the naive wiser) and direct instruction (the wise person simply receives and grows from teaching). Both are effective, but direct instruction is more efficient. The fool, notably, learns from neither.
verses.prayer: God, help me learn from every correction.
verses.discussion_question: What is something you learned by watching someone else's bad choice?
verses.family_discussion: How do we ensure our children learn from both observed consequences and direct teaching — and that we are providing both?
verses.do_it_today: When you see or hear about a bad outcome from a wrong choice today, pause and say: 'What can I learn from that?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A simple child watching from a distance as a mocker faces consequences, learning on their face; a wise child leaning in to receive instruction from a teacher, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The righteous man wisely considereth the house of the wicked: but God overthroweth the wicked for their wickedness.
verses.little_bible: The righteous person watches carefully and understands what happens to the wicked. God brings down the wicked because of their sin.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God brings down the wicked for their sin.
verses.meaning: The righteous person is not naive — they observe the house of the wicked with wisdom and understand that it is headed for ruin. But it is God who ultimately executes judgment on the wicked. The righteous need not act in vengeance; God handles it.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You to bring justice.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we let God handle justice instead of taking it ourselves?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to trust God with justice — not taking revenge, not becoming bitter, but watching and trusting that God sees and acts?
verses.do_it_today: If something unfair has happened to you, name it to God today. Tell Him: 'I trust You to handle this.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A righteous figure watching thoughtfully from a distance as a tall house of the wicked crumbles by divine action, solemn and just watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.
verses.little_bible: If you close your ears to the poor when they cry for help, one day you will cry for help. And no one will hear you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Ignoring the poor means no one hears you.
verses.meaning: This verse teaches the principle of reciprocal justice: how we treat others in their need will shape how our own cries are treated. To ignore the poor is not merely unkind — it has consequences. God hears the poor; those who stop their ears to them will find their own cries unanswered.
verses.prayer: God, open my ears to those who are hurting.
verses.discussion_question: What should you do when you see someone who needs help?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate active generosity and responsiveness in our children — not turning away from need but moving toward it?
verses.do_it_today: Look for one person today who needs help. Do not walk past them. Help them in whatever way you can.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking past a crying person with hands over ears, contrasted with a child stopping, kneeling down, and helping with warmth, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.
verses.little_bible: A quiet, private gift can calm someone who is angry. A gentle act given in secret can turn away great anger.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A quiet gift calms anger.
verses.meaning: This is an observation about human psychology and relationships: a private, discreet gift — given without fanfare — has the power to defuse anger and strong wrath. It is not teaching bribery but wisdom about how to de-escalate conflict with grace and generosity.
verses.prayer: God, help me be a peacemaker with kindness.
verses.discussion_question: How can being kind and generous help when someone is angry?
verses.family_discussion: How do we practise de-escalation in our family — using generosity, gentleness, and private kindness to calm conflict rather than fanning it?
verses.do_it_today: If there is tension between you and someone, do one quiet, kind thing for them — without telling anyone.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child quietly handing a small gift to an angry person, the anger melting away into calm warmth, gentle and peaceful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: It is joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction shall be to the workers of iniquity.
verses.little_bible: The just person finds joy in doing what is right. But for those who do wrong, doing right brings them to ruin.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Doing right brings joy to the just.
verses.meaning: For the righteous person, doing justice is not a burden — it is a joy. This reveals that character transformation has taken place: what God commands has become what the person delights in. For the wicked, however, justice is their enemy and brings them down.
verses.prayer: God, make doing right feel like joy to me.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever felt truly happy because you did the right thing?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children move from obedience-as-duty to obedience-as-delight — where doing right feels like joy, not like a burden?
verses.do_it_today: Do something right today — not because you have to, but because you want to. Notice how it feels.
verses.illustration_prompt: A joyful child doing something fair and right, light radiating around them in happiness, contrasted with a shadowed figure whose wrong ways are unraveling, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.
verses.little_bible: The person who wanders away from wisdom ends up with those who are lost. Turning away from wisdom is very serious.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wandering from wisdom leads to being lost.
verses.meaning: This is one of Proverbs' most solemn warnings: abandoning the way of wisdom leads to death — spiritual and ultimately physical. The 'congregation of the dead' is a vivid description of those who have permanently departed from the living path. Departing from wisdom is not a neutral drift — it has a deadly destination.
verses.prayer: God, keep me on the path of wisdom.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you wander too far from the safe path?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that small drifts from wisdom — small compromises — can lead to large destinations they never intended?
verses.do_it_today: If you have drifted even a small bit from wisdom, take one step back toward God's path today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A lone figure wandering off a bright road into shadow and mist, the bright path still visible behind them, a serious and solemn watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
verses.little_bible: The person who lives only for fun and pleasure will end up with nothing. Always choosing comfort over hard work leads to being poor.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Living only for pleasure leads to poverty.
verses.meaning: Pleasure and enjoyment are not sin in themselves — but loving pleasure above all else, making it the centre of life, leads to poverty. It displaces the diligence and self-discipline that produce fruitful living. This is a warning against a life organised around self-indulgence.
verses.memory_phrase: Do not live just for fun.
verses.prayer: God, help me love what truly matters.
verses.discussion_question: Why is only wanting fun and comfort not a good way to live?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children enjoy pleasures rightly while not making pleasure their chief aim — cultivating both enjoyment and self-discipline?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one time today when you could take the easy, fun option. Choose the diligent one instead. See how it feels.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child choosing to play instead of work, fun things piling up around them but an empty bowl on the table, a gentle warning in the watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.
verses.little_bible: Sometimes the wicked person ends up suffering what the righteous person was going to face. God protects the righteous. The wrongdoer bears the result of their wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God protects the righteous from harm.
verses.meaning: This proverb describes a pattern of providential justice in history: the wicked sometimes end up suffering the very harm they intended for the righteous. God's governance of history means the righteous are not ultimately abandoned to the malice of those who oppose them. This does not mean the righteous never suffer — but wickedness aimed at the righteous can be deflected back onto its source.
verses.prayer: God, protect me when others mean me harm.
verses.discussion_question: How has God ever protected someone you love from harm?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children trust in God's protection — not as a magic shield against all pain, but as the deep security that He governs even harmful situations?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God for one time He protected you or someone you love — even if you only saw it later.
verses.illustration_prompt: A gentle divine shield deflecting harm away from a righteous child, the harm falling back instead on the one who sent it, protective golden watercolour scene

verses.kjv: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.
verses.little_bible: It is better to live alone in the wilderness than in a home full of arguing and anger. A peaceful home is a treasure.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A peaceful home is precious.
verses.meaning: Paired with verse 9, this proverb again emphasises that peace in the home is more valuable than any material comfort. A contentious, angry spirit poisons the atmosphere of a home, making even a pleasant house feel like a wilderness. The lesson is universal — cultivate peace in your home.
verses.prayer: God, make our home a place of peace.
verses.discussion_question: What does a home full of peace feel like?
verses.family_discussion: What practices, habits, or conversations are creating peace in our home — and which ones are creating conflict? How can we shift the balance?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to be a peaceful presence in your home today. When tempted to argue, be the one who is gentle instead.
verses.illustration_prompt: A lonely figure sitting peacefully in a wilderness under the stars, more content than someone trapped in a house where angry voices echo, calm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.
verses.little_bible: The home of the wise has treasure and good things stored up. But a foolish person spends everything and has nothing left.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wise store up. The foolish spend all.
verses.meaning: Wisdom produces stores — not hoard-level selfishness, but the habit of provision, saving, and stewardship. The foolish person consumes everything without thought, leaving nothing. This is a proverb about financial and practical wisdom, but also about the broader pattern of stewarding what God gives.
verses.prayer: God, help me be wise with what I have.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be wise with the things you have been given?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children the basics of stewardship — saving, sharing, and spending wisely — as an expression of wisdom, not just financial skill?
verses.do_it_today: Set aside a small amount of something today — time, money, or energy — as a wise store for tomorrow.
verses.illustration_prompt: A cosy dwelling with a glowing store of treasure and oil, a wise family caring for it; a foolish figure with empty hands and empty shelves, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
verses.little_bible: Chasing after what is right and showing kindness leads to real life. It leads to honour and goodness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Follow righteousness and mercy — find life.
verses.meaning: This is one of Proverbs' great positive promises. The person who actively pursues righteousness (right living before God) and mercy (covenant kindness to others) receives life, righteousness, and honour. These are not just earthly rewards — they are the very things pursued become the reward.
verses.prayer: God, help me follow what is right and kind.
verses.discussion_question: What do you think it means to follow righteousness and mercy?
verses.family_discussion: How do we actively pursue righteousness and mercy as a family — making them the things we chase, not just the things we admire?
verses.do_it_today: Do one act of mercy today — a kind, undeserved act toward someone. Follow it up with one right and honest choice.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child running joyfully on a bright path labeled righteousness and mercy, finding treasure of life and honour at the end, warm glowing watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
verses.little_bible: One wise person can climb over the defences of a powerful city. Wisdom is stronger than great strength.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wisdom overcomes great strength.
verses.meaning: Military strength and fortifications seem unbeatable, but wisdom finds the way through or over them. This is a proverb about the surprising power of wisdom over brute force — brain over brawn. The mightiest defences in the world cannot withstand someone with genuine wisdom.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom stronger than any wall.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time when being smart and wise won over just being big and strong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that wisdom is not weakness — it is, in fact, the most powerful force available to them?
verses.do_it_today: When you face something hard today, ask: 'What is the wise way to handle this?' instead of just pushing harder.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small, thoughtful child confidently scaling the walls of a great fortress city, wisdom guiding every step, amazed soldiers looking on, adventurous watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.
verses.little_bible: Guard what you say. Keeping your mouth and tongue safe keeps your whole soul safe from trouble.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Guarding your words guards your soul.
verses.meaning: Speech is so directly connected to the soul's health and safety that guarding the mouth is equivalent to protecting the soul. This is not just social wisdom — it is spiritual wisdom. What we say reflects what we are and shapes what we experience.
verses.prayer: God, help me guard what I say today.
verses.discussion_question: How can the words you say get you into trouble?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate the habit of thinking before speaking in our children — and ourselves — as a genuine spiritual discipline, not just good manners?
verses.do_it_today: Before every sentence today, ask: 'Is this good to say?' Pause. Then speak — or stay quiet.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a gentle hand near their mouth, choosing words carefully, a protective light around their soul as a result, peaceful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Proud and haughty scorner is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.
verses.little_bible: The person who mocks others with pride and anger has a name: proud, haughty scorner. That is who they are.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Pride and mockery define the scorner.
verses.meaning: The scorner is here defined not just by what they do but by what they are. Their name is 'proud and haughty' — pride is their identity and their operating mode. This is a solemn description: a person can become what they repeatedly choose, and pride ultimately defines them.
verses.prayer: God, keep pride and mockery far from me.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be a proud person who mocks others?
verses.family_discussion: How do we identify and address a mocking spirit in our children early — before it becomes who they are rather than just what they do?
verses.do_it_today: If you have mocked anyone recently — even in your mind — stop and replace that thought with something kind.
verses.illustration_prompt: A proud, haughty figure looking down on others with a mocking expression, a shadow of pride surrounding them, solemn and clear watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.
verses.little_bible: The lazy person wants things but will not work for them. That wanting without working destroys them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Lazy wanting without working destroys.
verses.meaning: The sluggard's problem is not lack of desire — they desire! But their hands refuse to work for what they want. This gap between desire and effort is the source of their destruction. Wanting good things is not enough; you must be willing to work.
verses.prayer: God, give me willing hands to work.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between wanting something and working to get it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children the habit of connecting desire with effort — teaching that wanting is only the beginning, and willing work must follow?
verses.do_it_today: Name one thing you want. Then do one thing today that moves you toward it through honest work.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child lying down wanting good things but with hands folded refusing to move, the good things staying out of reach, gentle but serious watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
verses.little_bible: The greedy person wants more and more all day long. But the righteous person gives freely and holds nothing back.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The righteous give freely all day.
verses.meaning: The contrast is sharp: endless greedy craving on one side, and generous, unstinting giving on the other. The righteous person is not defined by what they accumulate but by what they give away. Generosity is a mark of righteousness.
verses.memory_phrase: Give freely; do not hold back.
verses.prayer: God, make me a generous giver today.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between always wanting more and freely giving to others?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate generosity as a daily rhythm in our family — not just as occasional giving events but as a consistent orientation of our lives?
verses.do_it_today: Give something away freely today — your time, something you own, or help you could offer. Hold nothing back.
verses.illustration_prompt: A righteous child with open hands giving generously, light streaming from them; a greedy figure clutching things tightly with hungry eyes, watercolour contrast

verses.kjv: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
verses.little_bible: God hates it when wicked people bring offerings to Him. It is even worse when they do it with evil thoughts in their hearts.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God hates offerings from wicked hearts.
verses.meaning: Religious performance by someone living in wickedness is not just neutral — it is an abomination to God. God is not interested in ritual without righteousness. The verse intensifies: when the wicked person brings sacrifice with deliberate wrongdoing in mind (perhaps using religion to cover their sin), the offence is even greater.
verses.memory_phrase: God sees your heart, not just offerings.
verses.prayer: God, make my heart clean before I worship.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God care about what is in our hearts when we pray or worship?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that God wants genuine worship from a clean heart — not religious performance that hides a life lived wrongly?
verses.do_it_today: Before praying or reading the Bible today, ask God to clean your heart first. Then come to Him honestly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure bringing an offering while hiding something dark behind their back, God's light turning away from the offering, solemn and honest watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.
verses.little_bible: The person who lies as a witness will be destroyed. But the person who truly listens tells the truth steadily and always.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Listen truly; speak truth always.
verses.meaning: False testimony — lying about what you witnessed — leads to ruin. But the person who genuinely listens — who takes in what actually happened before speaking — gives reliable, constant testimony. True listening produces truthful speaking. This is a wisdom connection between the inner life (listening) and the outer testimony (speaking).
verses.prayer: God, help me only speak what is true.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to listen carefully before you speak?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate truthfulness in our children — not just not lying, but speaking with reliability and precision, and listening before speaking?
verses.do_it_today: Before speaking about anyone or anything today, make sure you have really heard and understood. Then speak the truth.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure caught lying with their words crumbling away; a careful listener leaning in to hear, then speaking clearly and steadily with truth shining around them, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but as for the upright, he directeth his way.
verses.little_bible: The wicked person has a hard, stubborn face. But the upright person is honest and keeps their way straight.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The upright keep their way straight.
verses.meaning: Hardening the face is a picture of stubborn defiance — pushing back against correction, truth, and accountability. The upright person, by contrast, considers their way — they examine, direct, and adjust their path. Openness to correction is a mark of uprightness.
verses.memory_phrase: Stay open and keep your way right.
verses.prayer: God, keep my face soft and my heart open.
verses.discussion_question: What does a hard, stubborn face tell you about someone's heart?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children remain open to correction and direction — not hardening against accountability but staying teachable and honest about their path?
verses.do_it_today: When someone corrects you today, choose a soft, open response instead of a hard, defensive one.
verses.illustration_prompt: A stubborn figure with a hardened, closed face refusing to look; an upright child with a gentle open face, carefully walking a straight path, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.
verses.little_bible: No wisdom, no plan, no advice can stand against God. Nothing and no one is stronger than God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Nothing stands against God.
verses.meaning: This verse is an absolute declaration of God's sovereignty over all human wisdom, understanding, and counsel. No matter how clever the strategy, how sophisticated the plan, or how wise the advisor — nothing can succeed against God. This is both a warning to those who oppose Him and a comfort to those who trust Him.
verses.prayer: God, You are above all wisdom and plans.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean that nothing can stand against God?
verses.family_discussion: How does the truth that no wisdom or plan can succeed against God reshape the way we make decisions, face opposition, and seek His counsel?
verses.do_it_today: When you face a decision today, ask God first. Remember: His counsel is the only one that cannot fail.
verses.illustration_prompt: All human wisdom and plans as small structures against the vast, immovable presence of God, everything human dwarfed by His greatness, majestic watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the LORD.
verses.little_bible: You can get ready. You can prepare everything. But only God gives true safety. Safety comes from God alone.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Prepare well, but trust God for safety.
verses.meaning: The final verse of the chapter is one of Proverbs' great theological conclusions. Preparation is not condemned — you prepare the horse. But the outcome — safety and victory — belongs to God alone. This is the balance of biblical wisdom: use every resource God has given you, while trusting the result entirely to Him. This verse has comforted God's people before battles, before exams, before surgeries, before countless uncertain moments.
verses.prayer: God, I prepare and I trust You for safety.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we trust God even when we have prepared well?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate both diligent preparation and deep God-trust in our children — so they neither become passive (not preparing) nor self-reliant (not trusting)?
verses.do_it_today: Before something you are preparing for, do your very best preparation — then pray: 'God, the safety is Yours. I trust You.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A strong horse prepared and ready for battle, a rider poised — but above them a great divine light covering everything, the true source of safety and victory, glowing watercolour scene
